mechanism_variables: Resting tonic vagal tone (RMSSD, HF-HRV power)
Phasic sympathetic reactivity (EDA peak amplitude, SCR frequency during standardized stressor)
Sensor noise floor (PPG signal quality index, EDA baseline noise variance)
Stress detection uncertainty (classifier predictive entropy, false negative rate per subject)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Low tonic vagal tone → reduced HRV amplitude during stress → HRV features fall below sensor noise floor → feature extraction yields low signal-to-noise ratio → classifier misclassifies stress as non-stress → increased false negative rate and predictive entropy for that subject
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between baseline ANS reactivity (tonic vagal tone, phasic sympathetic reactivity) and stress-detection uncertainty (higher uncertainty for blunted responders)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Wearable sensor type (PPG/EDA) with known noise floors
Stressor intensity sufficient to elicit ANS response in typical individuals
Resting baseline measured under controlled conditions (supine, 5-min)
Exclusion of cardiovascular/respiratory medication users
measurable_outcomes: Subject-level false negative rate (FNR) for stress epochs
Predictive entropy of stress classifier per subject
Correlation between resting RMSSD and FNR
Signal-to-noise ratio of HRV/EDA features during stress vs. non-stress
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Need to quantify sensor-specific noise floors and define 'blunted' reactivity thresholds using population percentiles; consider multi-sensor fusion to mitigate single-channel noise.

mechanism_variables: Skin melanin index (spectrophotometry at 650nm)
Stratum corneum thickness (confocal microscopy)
Skin hydration (corneometry)
Hair density (trichoscopy)
PPG signal quality index (SQI) during rest and stress
EDA contact impedance (kΩ)
Stress classifier uncertainty (predictive entropy, confidence interval width)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Higher melanin index → reduced PPG light penetration → lower PPG perfusion signal amplitude → increased motion artifact susceptibility → classifier interprets noise as physiological variability → inflated predictive entropy for high-melanin subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between melanin index/stratum corneum thickness and stress-detection uncertainty (higher uncertainty for darker/thicker skin)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Green-light PPG wavelength (e.g., 530nm) and EDA electrode material (Ag/AgCl)
Controlled ambient light and temperature
Standardized sensor placement (wrist, dorsal)
Exclusion of skin pathologies (eczema, psoriasis)
measurable_outcomes: Subject-level PPG SQI and EDA impedance
Classifier predictive entropy per subject
Correlation between melanin index and predictive entropy
False positive/negative rates stratified by skin phenotype quartiles
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Need to disentangle skin phenotype effects from motion artifact; consider multi-wavelength PPG (green + infrared) to isolate melanin attenuation.

mechanism_variables: Chronotype (MEQ score, dim light melatonin onset - DLMO)
Circadian phase at stressor (hours since DLMO, or clock time)
Salivary cortisol awakening response (CAR) magnitude
HRV/EDA reactivity to standardized stressor at different times
Classifier stress probability output
Prediction error (difference between classifier probability and ground truth)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Morning chronotype + morning stressor → amplified sympathetic reactivity → larger HRV/EDA feature changes → classifier correctly detects stress (low uncertainty). Morning chronotype + evening stressor → blunted reactivity → smaller feature changes → classifier misclassifies (high uncertainty). Reverse for evening types.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Interaction effect: uncertainty highest when chronotype and stressor timing are misaligned (e.g., morning type in evening, evening type in morning)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Free-living vs. lab stressors
Controlled light exposure prior to measurement
Exclusion of shift workers, recent transmeridian travel
Classifier trained on pooled time-of-day data without circadian features
measurable_outcomes: Subject-level calibration error (ECE) as function of circadian phase × chronotype
AUC-ROC per subject per time-of-day bin
Correlation between MEQ score and time-of-day uncertainty slope
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Need to measure circadian phase directly (DLMO) rather than rely on clock time; consider adding time-of-day as explicit feature in classifier.

mechanism_variables: Emotion regulation strategy use (ERQ suppression/reappraisal subscales, state ERQ)
Subjective stress rating (EMA, 0-100 VAS)
HRV (RMSSD, LF/HF), EDA (SCR rate, amplitude), cardiovascular (HR, BP) during stress
Classifier predicted stress probability
Label-physiology discrepancy (residual between predicted and reported stress)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High suppression → amplified cardiovascular reactivity + dampened EDA → wearable features (HRV, EDA) show mixed pattern → classifier trained on typical stress physiology (high HR, low HRV, high EDA) yields uncertain prediction → high predictive entropy for high suppressors
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between suppression tendency and stress-detection uncertainty (predictive entropy); negative correlation for reappraisal
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Standardized stress induction (e.g., TSST, cognitive load)
Concurrent EMA and wearable recording
Control for baseline affect (PANAS)
Classifier features include both cardiovascular and EDA modalities
measurable_outcomes: Subject-level predictive entropy
Correlation between ERQ suppression score and entropy
Feature importance shift for high vs. low regulators
Calibration curves stratified by regulation strategy
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Need to distinguish trait vs. state regulation; consider multi-modal features and regulation-aware labeling.

mechanism_variables: Non-wear episodes (accelerometer-based detection, timestamp, duration)
Self-reported stress during non-wear (retrospective EMA)
Observed stress classifier uncertainty during wear periods
True stress exposure (EMA including non-wear recall)
Imputation method (mean, last observation, model-based)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High stress event → device removal → missing high-stress epochs → observed data lacks peak stress → classifier trained/calibrated on observed data underestimates stress probability for that subject → uncertainty estimates biased downward for high-stress subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between stress-correlated non-wear frequency and observed uncertainty (downward bias); positive correlation for low-stress subjects (upward bias due to overrepresentation of low-stress data)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Wearable with accelerometer for non-wear detection
EMA prompts random and event-contingent
Non-wear reasons logged (survey)
Analysis restricted to subjects with >20% non-wear time
measurable_outcomes: Bias in subject-level predictive entropy (observed vs. true with imputed ground truth)
Correlation between non-wear during high-stress EMA and entropy bias
Calibration error before/after multiple imputation
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Requires ground truth stress during non-wear (e.g., retrospective recall, proxy measures); consider pattern-mixture models for informative missingness.

mechanism_variables: Respiratory rate and depth (thoracic impedance, accelerometry)
RSA magnitude (HF-HRV power during paced breathing)
Vagal tone index (HRV during controlled breathing)
HRV stress reactivity (change in RMSSD/HF from baseline to stress)
Classifier uncertainty (predictive entropy) for HRV-only model
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Shallow/fast breathing → low RSA coupling → low baseline HF-HRV despite normal vagal tone → stress-induced vagal withdrawal produces smaller absolute HF change → HRV features show attenuated stress response → classifier yields high uncertainty (low confidence) for weak-coupling subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between RSA coupling strength (RSA per unit vagal tone) and stress-detection uncertainty for HRV-based classifiers
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Controlled breathing vs. free breathing
Paced breathing protocol to assess coupling (0.25 Hz)
Exclusion of respiratory disorders (asthma, COPD)
Classifier uses only HRV features (no respiration input)
measurable_outcomes: Subject-level RSA coupling coefficient (HF-HRV / respiratory depth)
Correlation between coupling coefficient and classifier entropy
Calibration error for weak vs. strong couplers
Improvement in uncertainty with respiration-augmented model
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Need to measure respiration concurrently; consider individual breathing patterns during stress; RSA coupling may be state-dependent.

mechanism_variables: Wrist circumference (mm)
Bone prominence (ultrasound or anthropometry)
Device tightness preference (self-report, or measured via strap tension sensor)
PPG signal quality index (SQI) during rest and activity
EDA contact impedance (kΩ)
Motion artifact magnitude (accelerometer variance)
Stress classifier uncertainty per subject
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Loose wear → high motion artifact + low perfusion → PPG features noisy → classifier uncertainty high. Tight wear → venous congestion → altered pulse waveform morphology (e.g., increased pulse transit time, changed amplitude) → feature bias → misclassification → high uncertainty. Optimal tightness minimizes both.
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: U-shaped relationship between tightness and uncertainty; also moderated by wrist circumference/bone prominence
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Specific wearable model (strap design, sensor geometry)
Controlled activity protocols (sedentary, walking, stress)
Standardized placement instructions vs. habitual wear
Exclusion of vascular pathologies
measurable_outcomes: Subject-level PPG SQI and EDA impedance
Correlation between tightness preference and predictive entropy
Feature distribution shift (mean, variance) across tightness levels
Uncertainty reduction with personalized calibration
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Need objective tightness measurement (e.g., pressure sensor); consider dynamic tightness changes during activity.

mechanism_variables: Allostatic load index (composite: hair cortisol, CRP, HbA1c, BP, waist-hip ratio, HDL)
Acute stress reactivity (HRV, EDA, cortisol response to TSST)
Feature dynamic range (max-min of HRV/EDA during stress vs. baseline)
Within-subject feature variance (stress and non-stress epochs)
Classifier predictive entropy per subject
Class separation (Mahalanobis distance between stress/non-stress feature clusters)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High allostatic load → blunted autonomic reactivity → smaller feature changes during stress → reduced class separation + increased within-class variance → classifier decision boundary overlaps both classes → high predictive entropy
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between allostatic load index and stress-detection uncertainty (predictive entropy); negative correlation with class separation
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Validated allostatic load composite (minimum 6 biomarkers)
Standardized acute stressor (TSST)
Free-living wearable data for classifier training
Exclusion of acute illness, medication affecting ANS
measurable_outcomes: Subject-level predictive entropy vs. allostatic load
Class separation metrics per subject
Calibration error stratified by allostatic load tertiles
Feature variance ratios (within/between stress conditions)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Allostatic load measurement requires multiple biomarkers; consider longitudinal design to establish causality.

mechanism_variables: Interoceptive awareness (MAIA score, heartbeat counting task accuracy)
EMA prompt timing and response
Physiological features (HRV, EDA) in windows pre- and post-EMA
Stress label (EMA rating)
Classifier uncertainty (predictive entropy) for epochs near EMA
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High interoceptive awareness → EMA prompt directs attention to body → amplified physiological reactivity post-prompt → wearable features during post-prompt window correlate with label (which was just given) → classifier learns spurious association → uncertainty estimates contaminated (overconfident for high awareness, underconfident for low)
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: For high awareness: lower uncertainty (overconfidence) for post-EMA epochs; for low awareness: higher uncertainty. Overall, subject-level uncertainty correlates with interoceptive awareness.
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: EMA prompt frequency and randomness
Control for stressor timing relative to EMA
Physiological recording continuous
Classifier trained on data including post-EMA windows
measurable_outcomes: Difference in predictive entropy for pre- vs. post-EMA windows by awareness group
Correlation between MAIA score and entropy bias
Feature-label correlation in post-EMA window vs. baseline
Calibration error with/without post-EMA data exclusion
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Need to isolate EMA reactivity from true stress; consider control prompts (non-stress questions) to measure attention effect.

mechanism_variables: Subject-specific baseline (intercept) for HRV/EDA
Subject-specific stress reactivity (slope)
Subject-specific autocorrelation (AR1 parameter)
Population-level classifier predictive distribution (mean, variance)
Hierarchical model (mixed-effects) predictive distribution
Calibration metrics: expected calibration error (ECE) per subject, prediction interval coverage
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Ignoring random effects → model pools all subjects → estimates single residual variance → for high-variability subjects, true within-subject variance > pooled estimate → predictive intervals too narrow (anti-conservative); for low-variability subjects, true within-subject variance < pooled estimate → intervals too wide (over-conservative)
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between subject-level residual variance and prediction interval coverage (high variability → under-coverage); positive correlation for low variability
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Sufficient repeated measures per subject (>50 stress/non-stress epochs)
Hierarchical model correctly specified (random intercepts, slopes, AR1)
Comparison between flat (pooled) and hierarchical models
Stressors varied in type/intensity
measurable_outcomes: Per-subject ECE for flat vs. hierarchical model
Prediction interval coverage probability per subject
Correlation between subject-level variance components and coverage bias
Log-likelihood improvement with hierarchical model
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Requires multilevel modeling framework; consider Bayesian hierarchical models for uncertainty quantification; test with cross-validation.
